app.title: PULL FOR PAIN
app.tagline: One lever. No typing. No checkbox grids.
app.deploy: static index.html at repo root, branch auto-deploys to <branch>-intake-oop.fly.dev
app.disclaimer: Fiction. LLM-generated parody patient. Not medical advice.
app.constraint: The patient cannot type and will not read a list. Every question is one pull and one answer.
app.covers: Every field on the clinic's paper form (patients/persistent-pain/intake-form.json). name, date_of_birth, address and phone are confirmed together as one pull, since a lever cannot spell. date is stamped automatically.
app.why_a_reel_beats_a_checkbox: A 15-box grid is skimmed in two seconds and answered wrong. A reel shows one option, alone, in big type, worded the way the patient would say it — and one pull commits it.

reel_modes.spin_to_pick: Reel spins through every option, lands on one. That is the answer.
reel_modes.spin_scale: Reel is 0-10. Lands on a number.

one_question_one_pull: Every question takes exactly one pull and gives exactly one answer.

questions.label: FILLED OUT BY
questions.printed_as: Filled out by (if not the patient)
questions.care_team_note: Paper says the wife filled it in and signed it. He is sitting right there. At some point in eighteen months he stopped answering for himself.

questions.label: NAME / DOB / ADDRESS / PHONE
questions.printed_as: Name, Date of birth, Address, Phone
questions.prompt: We have you as Fig Turnip, born 14 March 1965, 12 Garden Row, 555-0143. Still right?
questions.care_team_note: A lever can't spell a surname. The clinic already holds these four, so the pull confirms them instead of collecting them. The phone on file is his wife's.

questions.label: INSURANCE

reel.label: My wife's work
reel.flag: Paper says 'through my work'. The plan is his wife's, through her employer.

questions.care_team_note: His wife wrote 'through my work' on a form she was filling in for him, so the words came out of her mouth about her job. Billing finds out eleven days later.

questions.label: MEMBER ID
questions.prompt: Do you have the insurance card with you?
questions.care_team_note: Left blank on paper. A blank tells you nothing; 'it's at home' tells the front desk to stop waiting for it.

questions.label: EMERGENCY CONTACT
questions.prompt: If something happened, who should we call?
questions.care_team_note: Her number is also the number on file for him. In an emergency the clinic rings the person already in the room.

questions.label: REASON FOR VISIT
questions.care_team_note: Six lines of space on paper, four characters used. The reel only offers sentences, so a sentence is what comes back.

questions.label: PAIN RIGHT NOW
questions.care_team_note: The paper form has no pain scale at all, on a form handed to a man with eighteen months of pain visits. His scores have sat between 6 and 9 the whole time.

questions.label: CURRENT MEDICATIONS
questions.printed_as: Current medications (include over-the-counter, vitamins, eye drops, inhalers)
questions.prompt: Of the pills you were given — which one have you stopped, or skip?
questions.paper_answer: metformin, the nerve pill, meloxicam, tylenol

reel.label: The mood one
reel.plain_language: small white pill — stopped months ago
reel.flag: STOPPED. Nobody at the clinic knows. He listed four medications, the chart has five, this is the missing one.

reel.label: The nerve one
reel.plain_language: three a day, makes him foggy
reel.flag: Skips it on days he has things to do. Reads as non-response to treatment.

reel.label: The muscle one at night
reel.flag: Finished it in 2025. Still listed Active on the med list.

questions.care_team_note: The highest-value pull on the form. Asking what he takes returns a list that matches the chart. Asking which one he STOPPED returns the sertraline — the one fact nobody has. He keeps every pill in one bottle, so the reel names them the way he does.

questions.label: ALLERGIES
questions.prompt: Any medicine that's ever made you feel bad?

reel.label: Codeine — made me sick
reel.flag: Wrote 'none' on paper. Chart has CODEINE — NAUSEA in red at the top.

questions.care_team_note: He doesn't think nausea counts as an allergy. Most people don't. The word 'allergy' loses it; 'made you feel bad' recovers it.

questions.label: PAST CONDITIONS
questions.prompt: Besides the diabetes — what else are you being treated for?

reel.label: Something for my mood or nerves
reel.plain_language: he would never call this 'depression / anxiety'
reel.flag: He is prescribed sertraline. He did not tick this box — it is printed one row below the box he did tick.

questions.care_team_note: 15 boxes offered, 1 ticked, 2 true. 'Depression / anxiety' is a phrase he skims past. 'Something for my mood or nerves' is a phrase he answers.

questions.label: PAST SURGERIES

reel.label: My knee, a few years back

questions.care_team_note: Paper asked for procedure AND year and got 'knee'. The year was in the chart the whole time, four feet away.

questions.label: FAMILY HISTORY
questions.prompt: Anything that runs in the family?
questions.care_team_note: Two words on paper for a question about an entire family. One pull gets the same fact without the blank space that shames people into writing less.

questions.label: TOBACCO
questions.care_team_note: The paper form prints a blank line for the quit date and he walked straight past it. The reel splits 'quit' into long-ago and recent, which is the only part of the date that changes anything.

questions.label: ALCOHOL
questions.care_team_note: Paper offered three boxes and he invented a fourth answer: 'some'. On a reel there is no margin to write in, so the answer lands inside the options the clinic can actually use.

questions.label: RECREATIONAL DRUGS
questions.prompt: Anything else you take that a doctor didn't give you?
questions.care_team_note: The one question on the paper form he answered exactly as designed.

questions.label: SIGNATURE
questions.prompt: Last one. Are these your answers?

reel.label: Yes — mine
reel.flag: Paper was signed by his wife. These answers he gave himself.

questions.care_team_note: The paper form was signed 'O. Turnip (wife)'. If he pulls this one himself, it is the first thing in eighteen months that is his own answer, in his own hand, so to speak.

questions.label: SLEEP

reel.label: Badly. For a long time now.

questions.care_team_note: He isn't sleeping and has never been asked, because the paper form has no box for it. One pull and it's in the chart.

questions.label: WHAT HE WANTS
questions.prompt: What do you actually want to talk about?
questions.care_team_note: He will pick the fence. Let him. It is the only question on this form he has ever wanted to answer, and everything else comes out on the way there.

handoff.title: Three seconds before you walk in
handoff.rule: Only mismatches print. Agreement is silent.

lines.text: CODEINE allergy — the paper form says 'none'
SERTRALINE stopped months ago. Not on his list. Still Active in your chart.
GABAPENTIN skipped on active days (foggy) — not a treatment failure, a dosing problem
Depression/anxiety never ticked on paper. Reel caught it.
Insurance is his wife's plan, not his — paper says 'through my work'
Not sleeping. Never asked before today.
He wants to talk about the fence.
